title.zh: 卷37 司馬休之 司馬楚之 司馬景之 司馬叔璠 司馬天助
title.en: Volume 37: Sima Xiuzhi, Sima Chuzhi, Siman Jingzhi, Sima Shufan, Sima Tianzhu
title.raw: 卷37 司馬休之 司馬楚之 司馬景之 司馬叔璠 司馬天助 Volume 37: Sima Xiuzhi, Sima Chuzhi, Siman Jingzhi, Sima Shufan, Sima Tianzhu

sentences.zh: 司馬休之 司馬楚之 司馬景之 司馬叔璠 司馬天助

translations.literal: Sima Xiuzhi, Sima Chuzhi, Sima Jingzhi, Sima Shufan, Sima Tianzhu
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiuzhi, Sima Chuzhi, Sima Jingzhi, Sima Shufan, and Sima Tianzhu

sentences.zh: 司馬休之，字季豫，本河內溫人，晉宣帝季弟譙王遜之後也。

translations.literal: Sima Xiuzhi, styled Jiyu, was originally a man of Wen in Henan, a descendant of Prince of Qiao Sima Yi, the younger brother of the fourth rank of Jin's Emperor Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiuzhi, whose courtesy name was Jiyu, was a native of Wen in Henan Commandery and a descendant of Prince of Qiao Sima Yi, the younger brother of Jin's Emperor Xuan.

sentences.zh: [1]司馬叡僭立江南，又以遜子孫襲封。

translations.literal: [1] When Sima Rui usurped the throne south of the Yangzi, he also had Yi's descendants inherit the fief.
translations.idiomatic: [1] When Sima Rui established his regime in the south, he allowed Yi's line to continue holding the princely title by inheritance.

sentences.zh: 至休之父恬，為司馬昌明鎮北將軍、青兗二州刺史。

translations.literal: By Xiuzhi's father Tian, he served Sima Changming as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Yan provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi's father Tian served under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Yan.

sentences.zh: 天興五年，休之為司馬德宗平西將軍、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianxing, Xiuzhi was made Sima Dezong's General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jing province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianxing, Xiuzhi held the posts of General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jing under Emperor An of Jin.

sentences.zh: [2]為桓玄逼逐，遂奔慕容德。

translations.literal: [2] Driven out by Huan Xuan, he then fled to Murong De.
translations.idiomatic: [2] Huan Xuan forced him from office, and he fled to Murong De.

sentences.zh: 劉裕誅玄後，還建鄴，裕復以休之為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: After Liu Yu executed Xuan, he returned to Jiankang; Yu again appointed Xiuzhi Inspector of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Yu killed Huan Xuan, Xiuzhi returned to Jiankang, and Liu Yu again made him Inspector of Jing.

sentences.zh: 休之頗得江漢人心，劉裕疑其有異志。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi had won considerable favor among the people of the Jiang and Han region; Liu Yu suspected he harbored a separate intent.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi had won strong loyalty in the Jiang and Han basin, and Liu Yu began to suspect disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 而休之子文思繼休之兄尚之為譙王，謀圖裕，裕執送休之，令自為其所。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Xiuzhi's son Wensi had succeeded Xiuzhi's elder brother Shangzhi as Prince of Qiao and plotted against Yu; Yu seized him and sent him to Xiuzhi, ordering Xiuzhi to deal with the matter himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi's son Wensi had inherited the title of Prince of Qiao from Xiuzhi's elder brother Shangzhi and plotted against Liu Yu. Liu Yu arrested Wensi and handed him to Xiuzhi, demanding that Xiuzhi punish him himself.

sentences.zh: 休之表廢文思，并與裕書陳謝。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi memorialized to depose Wensi and also wrote Yu a letter of apology.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi memorialized to strip Wensi of his rank and wrote Liu Yu a letter of apology.

sentences.zh: 神瑞中，裕收休之子文寶、兄子文祖，並殺之，乃率眾討休之。

translations.literal: During the Shenrui era, Yu seized Xiuzhi's son Wenbao and his brother's son Wenzu, killed them both, and then led troops to attack Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenrui era Liu Yu arrested Xiuzhi's son Wenbao and his nephew Wenzu, executed them both, and marched against Xiuzhi at the head of an army.

sentences.zh: 休之上表自陳於德宗，與德宗鎮北將軍魯宗之、宗之子竟陵太守軌等起兵討裕。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi submitted a memorial explaining himself to Dezong; with Dezong's General Who Pacifies the North Lu Zongzhi, Zongzhi's son Gui the Administrator of Jingling, and others he raised troops to attack Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi memorialized Emperor An in his own defense and, together with the emperor's General Who Pacifies the North Lu Zongzhi, Zongzhi's son Gui the Administrator of Jingling, and others, took up arms against Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 裕軍至江陵，休之不能敵，遂與軌奔襄陽。

translations.literal: When Yu's army reached Jiangling, Xiuzhi could not resist and fled with Gui to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu's army reached Jiangling, Xiuzhi could not hold his ground and fled with Gui to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 裕復進軍討之。

translations.literal: Yu again advanced his army to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu pressed the campaign and marched against them once more.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣長孫嵩屯河東，將為之援。

translations.literal: Taizong sent Changsun Song to encamp at Hedong, intending to aid them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingyuan sent Changsun Song to hold Hedong, planning to come to their aid.

sentences.zh: 時姚興征虜將軍姚成王、冠軍將軍司馬國璠亦將兵救之，不及而還。

translations.literal: At that time Yao Xing's General Who Captures Barbarians Yao Chengwang and Champion General Sima Guofan also led troops to rescue them but arrived too late and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing's General Who Captures Barbarians Yao Chengwang and Champion General Sima Guofan also marched to their relief, but arrived too late and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 休之遂與子文思及宗之等奔於姚興。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi then fled with his son Wensi, Zongzhi, and the others to Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi fled with his son Wensi, Lu Zongzhi, and their party to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 裕滅姚泓，休之與文思及德宗河間王子道賜，輔國將軍溫楷，竟陵內史魯軌，荊州治中韓延之、殷約，平西參軍桓謐、桓璲及桓溫孫道度、道子，勃海刁雍，陳郡袁式等數百人，皆將妻子詣嵩降。

translations.literal: When Yu destroyed Yao Hong, Xiuzhi, Wensi, Dezong's Prince of Hejian Daoci, Aid-the-State General Wen Kai, Jingling Interior Secretary Lu Gui, Jing province aides Han Yanzhi and Yin Yue, Pacify-the-West staff officers Huan Mi and Huan Lin and Huan Wen's grandsons Daodu and Daozi, Bohai's Diao Yong, Chen commandery's Yuan Shi, and several hundred others all brought wives and children to Song to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Yu destroyed Yao Hong, Xiuzhi and Wensi, together with Prince Daoci of Hejian, Aid-the-State General Wen Kai, Jingling Interior Secretary Lu Gui, Jing provincial aides Han Yanzhi and Yin Yue, Pacify-the-West staff officers Huan Mi and Huan Lin, Huan Wen's grandsons Daodu and Daozi, Diao Yong of Bohai, Yuan Shi of Chen commandery, and several hundred others, all came with their families to surrender to Changsun Song.

sentences.zh: 月餘，休之卒于嵩軍。

translations.literal: After more than a month, Xiuzhi died in Song's army.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a month later Xiuzhi died in Changsun Song's camp.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「司馬休之率其同義，萬里歸誠，雅操不遂，中年殞喪，朕甚愍焉。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Sima Xiuzhi led those of shared purpose in returning in sincerity from ten thousand li; his lofty conduct was not fulfilled, and in midlife he perished—I am deeply grieved."
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "Sima Xiuzhi led his companions in shared purpose across a thousand miles to submit in good faith. His noble aims were cut short and he died in his prime. We are deeply grieved."

sentences.zh: 其追贈征西大將軍、右光祿大夫，諡始平聲公。」

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded General Who Conquers the West and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness on the Right, with the posthumous title Duke of Shisheng of Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Conquers the West and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness on the Right, with the posthumous title Duke of Shisheng of Shiping.

sentences.zh: 子彌陀，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Moduo inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Moduo inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 以選尚臨涇公主，而辭以先取毗陵公竇瑾女。

translations.literal: By selection he was to marry the Princess of Linjing, but he declined on the grounds that he had already taken Duke of Piling Dou Jin's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: He was chosen to marry the Princess of Linjing but declined on the ground that he had already taken the daughter of Duke of Piling Dou Jin.

sentences.zh: 與瑾並坐祝詛伏誅。

translations.literal: He and Jin were both executed for sitting together in curse-ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He and Jin were both executed for practicing curse-rituals together.

sentences.zh: 司馬楚之，字德秀，晉宣帝弟太常馗之八世孫。

translations.literal: Sima Chuzhi, styled Dexiu, was the eighth-generation descendant of Grand Master of Ceremonies Kui, younger brother of Jin's Emperor Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Chuzhi, whose courtesy name was Dexiu, was an eighth-generation descendant of Grand Master of Ceremonies Kui, the younger brother of Jin's Emperor Xuan.

sentences.zh: 父榮期，司馬德宗梁益二州刺史，為其參軍楊承祖所殺。

translations.literal: His father Rongqi was Sima Dezong's Inspector of Liang and Yi provinces and was killed by his staff officer Yang Chengzu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Rongqi had been Inspector of Liang and Yi under Emperor An of Jin and was murdered by his staff officer Yang Chengzu.

sentences.zh: 楚之時年十七，送父喪還丹楊。

translations.literal: Chuzhi was then seventeen and escorted his father's coffin back to Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhi was seventeen at the time and escorted his father's coffin back to Danyang.

sentences.zh: 值劉裕誅夷司馬戚屬，叔父宣期、兄貞之並為所殺。

translations.literal: It happened that Liu Yu was executing the Sima clan and kin; his uncle Xuanqi and elder brother Zhenzhi were both killed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu was then purging the Sima clan, and Chuzhi's uncle Xuanqi and elder brother Zhenzhi were both among those killed.

sentences.zh: 楚之乃亡匿諸沙門中濟江。

translations.literal: Chuzhi then hid among monks and crossed the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhi hid among Buddhist monks and crossed the Yangzi to escape.

sentences.zh: 自歷陽西入義陽、竟陵蠻中。

translations.literal: From Liyang he went west into Yiyang and the Man country of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: From Liyang he made his way west into Yiyang and the tribal lands of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 及從祖荊州刺史休之為裕所敗，乃亡於汝潁之間。

translations.literal: When his collateral ancestor Xiuzhi the Inspector of Jing was defeated by Yu, he then wandered between the Ru and Ying rivers.
translations.idiomatic: When his kinsman Xiuzhi, Inspector of Jing, was defeated by Liu Yu, he took refuge in the region between the Ru and Ying.

sentences.zh: 楚之少有英氣，能折節待士。

translations.literal: Chuzhi from youth had heroic spirit and could humble himself to treat scholars.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Chuzhi had a bold spirit and knew how to win men by treating them with respect.

sentences.zh: 與司馬順明、道恭等所在聚黨。

translations.literal: With Sima Shunming, Daogong, and others he gathered factions wherever he went.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he went he gathered followers with Sima Shunming, Daogong, and others.

sentences.zh: 及劉裕自立，楚之規欲報復，收眾據長社，歸之者常萬餘人。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu declared himself [emperor], Chuzhi planned revenge, gathered followers, and held Changshe; those who joined him were often more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Yu seized the throne, Chuzhi plotted revenge, rallied supporters, and seized Changshe, where more than ten thousand men regularly joined him.

sentences.zh: 劉裕深憚之，遣刺客沐謙害楚之。

translations.literal: Liu Yu deeply feared him and sent the assassin Mu Qian to kill Chuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu feared him deeply and sent the assassin Mu Qian to kill him.

sentences.zh: 楚之待謙甚厚。

translations.literal: Chuzhi treated Qian very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhi treated Qian with great kindness.

sentences.zh: 謙夜詐疾，知楚之必自來，因欲殺之。

translations.literal: Qian at night feigned illness, knowing Chuzhi would surely come in person, and thus intended to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Qian feigned illness one night, knowing Chuzhi would visit in person, and planned to kill him then.

sentences.zh: 楚之聞謙病，果自齎湯藥往省之。

translations.literal: Chuzhi heard Qian was ill and indeed personally brought soup and medicine to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Qian was ill, Chuzhi did come in person, bringing soup and medicine to nurse him.

sentences.zh: 謙感其意，乃出匕首於席下，以狀告之曰：「將軍為裕所忌憚，願不輕率，以保全為先。

translations.literal: Qian was moved by his intent, then produced a dagger from beneath the mat and told him the facts, saying: "The general is feared and resented by Yu—please do not act rashly; put preservation first."
translations.idiomatic: Moved by this kindness, Qian drew a dagger from beneath the mat and confessed: "General, Liu Yu fears and hates you. Please do not act rashly; your safety must come first."

sentences.zh: 」楚之歎曰：「若如來言，雖有所防，恐有所失。

translations.literal: " Chuzhi sighed and said: "If it were as you say, though one took precautions, one would still fear missing something."
translations.idiomatic: " Chuzhi sighed and said: "Even if I took your advice and guarded myself, I would still fear failing in some way."

sentences.zh: 」謙遂委身以事之。

translations.literal: " Qian then devoted himself to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: " Qian then gave himself wholly to Chuzhi's service.

sentences.zh: 其推誠信物，得士之心，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His extending sincerity and trusting things to win men's hearts were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: In winning men's hearts through sincerity and trust, he was always like this.

sentences.zh: 太宗末，山陽公奚斤略地河南，楚之遣使請降。

translations.literal: At the end of Taizong's reign, Duke of Shanyang Xi Jin seized territory in Henan south of the river; Chuzhi sent envoys to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Emperor Mingyuan's reign, Duke of Shanyang Xi Jin was securing territory south of the Yellow River, and Chuzhi sent envoys to offer his surrender.

sentences.zh: 因表曰：「江淮以北，聞王師南首，無不抃舞，思奉德化。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: "North of the Jiang and Huai, hearing the royal army march south, none fail to clap and dance, longing to receive virtuous transformation."
translations.idiomatic: In his memorial he wrote: "North of the Jiang and Huai, wherever word spreads that the imperial army is marching south, the people clap and rejoice, yearning to receive your civilizing rule."

sentences.zh: 而逼於寇逆，無由自致。

translations.literal: "But pressed by bandits and rebels, they have no means to present themselves."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet pressed by rebels and invaders, they have had no way to reach you."

sentences.zh: 臣因民之欲，請率慕義為國前驅。

translations.literal: "Your subject, following the people's desire, asks to lead those who admire righteousness as vanguard for the state."
translations.idiomatic: "Your servant, acting on the people's wish, asks to lead those who embrace your cause as the army's vanguard."

sentences.zh: 今皆白衣，無以制服人望。

translations.literal: "Now we are all in plain dress and have no means to command men's regard."
translations.idiomatic: "We are all in plain dress and cannot yet command men's respect."

sentences.zh: 若蒙偏裨之號，假王威以唱義，則莫不率從。

translations.literal: "If we received a deputy-general's title and borrowed the king's authority to proclaim righteousness, none would fail to follow in throngs."
translations.idiomatic: "If you granted us a subordinate command and lent us your authority to raise the standard of loyalty, none would fail to follow."

sentences.zh: 」於是假楚之使持節、征南將軍、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Chuzhi was provisionally made Bearer of the Staff, General Who Conquers the South, and Inspector of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was then provisionally appointed Bearer of the Staff, General Who Conquers the South, and Inspector of Jing.

sentences.zh: 奚斤既平河南，以楚之所率戶民分置汝南、南陽、南頓、新蔡四郡，[4]以益豫州。

translations.literal: After Xi Jin had pacified Henan south of the river, the household population Chuzhi led was distributed into the four commanderies of Runan, Nanyang, Nandun, and Xincai [4] to augment Yu province.
translations.idiomatic: After Xi Jin pacified the south bank of the Yellow River, the households Chuzhi had led were settled in Runan, Nanyang, Nandun, and Xincai [4] to enlarge Yu province.

sentences.zh: 世祖初，楚之遣妻子內居於鄴，尋徵入朝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizu's reign, Chuzhi sent wife and children to live within at Ye, and soon was summoned to court.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Taiwu's reign Chuzhi sent his wife and children to live at Ye and was soon summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 時南藩諸將表劉義隆欲入為寇，以楚之為使持節、安南大將軍，封琅邪王，屯潁川以拒之。

translations.literal: At that time southern frontier generals reported that Liu Yilong intended to invade; Chuzhi was made Bearer of the Staff, Great General Who Pacifies the South, enfeoffed as Prince of Langye, and encamped at Yingchuan to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Southern commanders then reported that Liu Yilong planned an invasion. Chuzhi was made Bearer of the Staff and Great General Who Pacifies the South, enfeoffed as Prince of Langye, and stationed at Yingchuan to meet him.

sentences.zh: 其長史臨邑子步還表曰：「楚之渡河，百姓思舊，義眾雲集，汝潁以南，望風翕然，回首革面。

translations.literal: His Chief Clerk, Baron of Linyi Bu Huan, memorialized: "When Chuzhi crossed the river, the people recalled the old order; righteous masses gathered like clouds; south of the Ru and Ying, at the wind all turned together and changed face."
translations.idiomatic: His chief clerk, Baron of Linyi Bu Huan, wrote: "When Chuzhi crossed the river the people turned to the old allegiance and righteous bands gathered like clouds. South of the Ru and Ying all who heard the news turned as one to the new rule."

sentences.zh: 斯誠陛下應天順民，聖德廣被之所致也。

translations.literal: "This is truly because Your Majesty responds to Heaven and follows the people—sagely virtue broadly spread brings it about."
translations.idiomatic: "This is truly the fruit of Your Majesty's responding to Heaven and winning the people—your sagely virtue reaching far and wide."

sentences.zh: 」世祖大悅，璽書勞勉，賜前後部鼓吹。

translations.literal: " Shizu was greatly pleased, sent an imperial letter of encouragement, and bestowed front and rear guard musicians.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased, sent an imperial letter of praise and encouragement, and granted him front and rear guard musicians.

sentences.zh: 義隆將到彥之泝河而西，列守南岸，至於潼關。

translations.literal: Yilong's general Dao Yanzhi went upriver westward, arrayed guards along the south bank, and reached Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yilong's general Dao Yanzhi marched up the Yellow River westward, posting guards along the south bank as far as Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 及彥之等退走，楚之破其別軍於長社。

translations.literal: When Yanzhi and the others retreated in flight, Chuzhi defeated their detached force at Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanzhi and his men retreated, Chuzhi routed their detached force at Changshe.

sentences.zh: 又與冠軍將軍安頡攻滑臺，拔之，擒義隆將朱脩之、李元德及東郡太守申謨，俘萬餘人。

translations.literal: He also joined Champion General An Bi in attacking Huatai, took it, captured Yilong's generals Zhu Xiuzhi and Li Yuande and Dong commandery Administrator Shen Mo, and took more than ten thousand prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Champion General An Bi in attacking Huatai, captured the city, seized Yilong's generals Zhu Xiuzhi and Li Yuande and Dong commandery Administrator Shen Mo, and took more than ten thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 上疏曰：「臣奉命南伐，受任一方，而智力淺短，誠節未效，所以夙夜憂惶，忘寢與食。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial: "Your subject received orders for the southern campaign and was entrusted with one region, yet my wit and strength are shallow and short, and loyal effort has not shown effect—therefore day and night I am anxious and fearful, forgetting sleep and food."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Your servant was ordered south on campaign and entrusted with a single front, yet my wit and strength are limited and my loyal service has not yet borne fruit. Day and night I am anxious and fearful, forgetting sleep and food."

sentences.zh: 臣屢遣人至荊揚，所在陳說，具論天朝盛化之美，莫不忻承聖德，傾首北望。

translations.literal: "Your subject repeatedly sent men to Jing and Yang, explaining everywhere and setting forth in full the Heavenly Court's flourishing transformation's beauty—none failed to rejoice in receiving sagely virtue and bow their heads northward."
translations.idiomatic: "I have repeatedly sent men to Jing and Yang to proclaim everywhere the splendor of the Heavenly Court's rule. All rejoice to receive your sagely virtue and turn their faces north in hope."

sentences.zh: 而義隆兄弟知人情搖動，遣臣私讎順為司州刺史，統淮北七郡，代垣苗守懸瓠。

translations.literal: "But the Yilong brothers, knowing men's hearts were shaken, sent your subject's private enemy Shun as Inspector of Si province, commanding the seven commanderies north of the Huai, to replace Yuan Miao in guarding Xuange.
translations.idiomatic: "Yet the Yilong brothers, seeing that hearts were wavering, sent my personal enemy Shun as Inspector of Si to command the seven commanderies north of the Huai and replace Yuan Miao at Xuange."

sentences.zh: 自鞏、洛、滑臺敗散已來，義隆耻其敗北，多加罪罰。

translations.literal: "Since the defeats and dispersal at Gong, Luo, and Huatai, Yilong has been shamed by defeat in the north and has imposed many punishments."
translations.idiomatic: "Since the rout at Gong, Luoyang, and Huatai, Yilong has been shamed by defeat in the north and has punished many of his officers harshly."

sentences.zh: 到彥之削位，退同卒伍，殺姚縱夫於壽春，斬竺靈秀於彭城，王休元託疾，檀道濟斥放。

translations.literal: "Dao Yanzhi was stripped of rank and reduced to common soldier; Yao Zongfu was killed at Shouchun; Zhu Lingxiu was beheaded at Pengcheng; Wang Xiuyuan pleaded illness; Tan Daoji was expelled and sent away."
translations.idiomatic: "Dao Yanzhi was demoted to the ranks; Yao Zongfu was executed at Shouchun; Zhu Lingxiu was beheaded at Pengcheng; Wang Xiuyuan feigned illness; Tan Daoji was dismissed and sent away."

sentences.zh: 凡在腹心，悉懷疑阻。

translations.literal: "All who were in the inner circle harbored suspicion and obstruction alike."
translations.idiomatic: "Every man in his inner circle is now suspicious and obstructed."

sentences.zh: 民怨臣猜，可謂今日。

translations.literal: "Popular resentment and ministerial suspicion—this may be called the present day."
translations.idiomatic: "Popular resentment and mutual suspicion among his ministers—that is the state of things today."

sentences.zh: 臣聞平殄寇逆，必乘戰勝之威；

translations.literal: "Your subject has heard that to pacify and exterminate bandits and rebels one must ride the authority of victory in battle;"
translations.idiomatic: "I have heard that to crush rebels one must strike while victory's momentum is fresh;"

sentences.zh: 建立功勳，亦因離貳之勢。

translations.literal: "to establish merit and achievement also relies on the momentum of division and defection."
translations.idiomatic: "and that to win great merit one must exploit division and defection."

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下聖德膺符，道光四海，神旌所指，莫不摧服，其未賓者義隆而已。

translations.literal: "Bowingly considering that Your Majesty's sagely virtue received the mandate, your way illumines the four seas—where the divine banner points, none fail to be shattered and submit; only Yilong has not yet submitted."
translations.idiomatic: "Your sagely virtue has received Heaven's mandate and your radiance fills the four seas. Where your banner points, none can stand; only Yilong has not yet submitted."

sentences.zh: 今天網遐舉，殊方仰德。

translations.literal: "Now the heavenly net is cast far; distant regions look up to virtue."
translations.idiomatic: "Now Heaven's net is cast wide and distant lands look up to your virtue."

sentences.zh: 固宜掃清東南，齊一區宇，使濟濟之風，被於江漢。

translations.literal: "It is fitting to sweep clear the southeast, unite the realm, and let the abundant wind of culture spread over the Jiang and Han."
translations.idiomatic: "It is time to sweep the southeast clean, unite the realm, and let civilizing influence spread over the Jiang and Han."

sentences.zh: 」世祖以兵久勞，不從。

translations.literal: " The emperor, because the troops had long been weary, did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, seeing that the army had long been exhausted, did not agree.

sentences.zh: 以散騎常侍徵還。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhi was recalled to court as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 從征涼州，以功賜隸戶一百。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Liang province and for merit was granted one hundred dependent households.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the Liangzhou campaign and for his merit received one hundred dependent households.

sentences.zh: 義隆遣將裴方明、胡崇之寇仇池。

translations.literal: Yilong sent generals Pei Fangming and Hu Chongzhi to raid Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Yilong sent generals Pei Fangming and Hu Chongzhi to attack Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 以楚之為假節，與淮陽公皮豹子等督關中諸軍從散關西入，擊走方明，擒崇之。

translations.literal: Chuzhi was made with provisional staff and, with Duke of Huaiyang Pi Baozi and others, supervised all Guanzhong armies, entered west from San Pass, routed Fangming, and captured Chongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhi was given provisional authority and, with Duke of Huaiyang Pi Baozi and others, commanded the Guanzhong armies through San Pass, routed Fangming, and captured Chongzhi.

sentences.zh: 仇池平而還。

translations.literal: Chouchi was pacified and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: After Chouchi was pacified he returned.

sentences.zh: 車駕伐蠕蠕，詔楚之與濟陰公盧中山等督運以繼大軍。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned against the Rouran, an edict ordered Chuzhi with Duke of Jiyin Lu Zhongshan and others to supervise transport to follow the great army.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's campaign against the Rouran, Chuzhi was ordered with Duke of Jiyin Lu Zhongshan and others to supervise supply trains following the main army.

sentences.zh: 時鎮北將軍封沓亡入蠕蠕，說令擊楚之等以絕糧運。

translations.literal: At that time General Who Pacifies the North Feng Ta had fled into the Rouran and urged them to strike Chuzhi and the others to cut off grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Pacifies the North Feng Ta had defected to the Rouran and urged them to attack Chuzhi's column and cut off the grain supply.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕乃遣姦覘入楚之軍，截驢耳而去。

translations.literal: The Rouran then sent spies into Chuzhi's army, cut off donkeys' ears, and left.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran sent scouts into Chuzhi's camp, cut off donkeys' ears as a sign, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 有告失驢耳者，諸將莫能察。

translations.literal: When someone reported missing donkey ears, none of the generals could discern the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: When men reported missing donkey ears, none of the other generals understood what it meant.

sentences.zh: 楚之曰：「必是覘賊截之以為驗耳，賊將至矣。

translations.literal: Chuzhi said: "Surely spies cut them off as proof—the enemy will arrive soon."
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhi said: "Spies must have cut them off as proof that they had been here—the enemy will attack soon."

sentences.zh: 」即使軍人伐柳為城，水灌之令凍，城立而賊至。

translations.literal: " He immediately had soldiers cut willows for a wall, poured water to freeze it—the wall stood and the enemy arrived.
translations.idiomatic: He had his men cut willows and pack them into a wall, then poured water until it froze solid. The wall was finished just as the enemy arrived.

sentences.zh: 冰峻城固，不可攻逼，賊乃走散。

translations.literal: The ice was steep and the wall firm; they could not attack or press it, and the enemy then scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The ice was hard and the wall impregnable; unable to breach it, the enemy broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 世祖聞而嘉之。

translations.literal: Shizu heard and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of this and praised him.

sentences.zh: 長子寶胤，與楚之同入國。

translations.literal: His eldest son Baoyin entered the state together with Chuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Baoyin had entered the state together with Chuzhi.

sentences.zh: 拜中書博士、雁門太守。

translations.literal: He was appointed Erudite of the Secretariat and Administrator of Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Erudite of the Secretariat and Administrator of Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 延宗，父亡後數年卒。

translations.literal: Yanzong died several years after his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzong died a few years after his father.

sentences.zh: 子裔，字承業。

translations.literal: His son Yi, styled Chengye.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi, whose courtesy name was Chengye.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，悅等為裔理嫡，還襲祖爵。

translations.literal: During Shizong's time, Yue and others argued Yi's case as legitimate heir, and he returned to inherit the ancestral title.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowen, Yue and others upheld Yi's claim as legitimate heir, and he recovered the ancestral title.

sentences.zh: 位至後軍將軍。

translations.literal: He reached the post of General of the Rear Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General of the Rear Guard.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈征虜將軍、洛州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously awarded General Who Captures Barbarians and Inspector of Luo province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made General Who Captures Barbarians and Inspector of Luo.

sentences.zh: 子藏，襲。

translations.literal: His son Zang inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zang inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the mandate, by precedent his rank was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne, his rank was reduced in the usual way.

sentences.zh: 纂，字茂宗，中書博士。

translations.literal: Zuan, styled Maozong, was Erudite of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan, whose courtesy name was Maozong, was Erudite of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 歷司州治中、別駕，河內邑中正。

translations.literal: He successively served as Aide of Si province, Administrator's Assistant, and Rectifier of the He'nan community.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Aide of Si province, Administrator's Assistant, and Rectifier of the Henan community.

sentences.zh: 永平元年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Yongping.

sentences.zh: 贈鎮遠將軍、南青州刺史，諡曰肅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded General Who Pacifies the Distant and Inspector of South Qing province, with posthumous name Su.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made General Who Pacifies the Distant and Inspector of South Qing, with the posthumous name Su.

sentences.zh: 子澄，字元鏡。

translations.literal: His son Cheng, styled Yuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cheng, whose courtesy name was Yuanjing.

sentences.zh: 司州秀才，司空功曹參軍、給事中。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate of Si, he was Staff Officer in the Bureau of Merit of the Minister of Works and Attendant Within the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: A Si province graduate, he served as Staff Officer in the Bureau of Merit of the Minister of Works and as Attendant Within the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈龍驤將軍、夏州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously awarded General of Dragon Cavalry and Inspector of Xia province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made General of Dragon Cavalry and Inspector of Xia.

sentences.zh: 澄弟仲粲，武定中，尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Cheng's younger brother Zhongcan, during Wuding, was Left Assistant of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng's younger brother Zhongcan served as Left Assistant of the Masters of Writing during the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 悅，字慶宗。

translations.literal: Yue, styled Qingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Yue, whose courtesy name was Qingzong.

sentences.zh: 自司空司馬出為立節將軍、建興太守，轉寧朔將軍、司州別駕。

translations.literal: From Staff Officer of the Minister of Works he went out as General Who Establishes Integrity and Administrator of Jianxing, then transferred to General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator's Assistant of Si province.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving his post as Staff Officer of the Minister of Works, he became General Who Establishes Integrity and Administrator of Jianxing, then General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator's Assistant of Si.

sentences.zh: 遷太子左衞率、河北太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard and Administrator of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard and Administrator of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，除鎮遠將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distant and Inspector of Yu province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowen's reign he was made General Who Pacifies the Distant and Inspector of Yu.

sentences.zh: 時有汝南上蔡董毛奴者，齎錢五千，死在道路。

translations.literal: At that time there was one Dong Maonu of Shangcai in Runan, who carried five thousand cash and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a man named Dong Maonu of Shangcai in Runan was found dead on the road with five thousand cash on him.

sentences.zh: 郡縣疑民張堤為劫，又於堤家得錢五千。

translations.literal: The commandery and county suspected the commoner Zhang Di of robbery, and again found five thousand cash in Di's house.
translations.idiomatic: The local authorities suspected a commoner named Zhang Di of the robbery, and another five thousand cash was found in Di's home.

sentences.zh: 堤懼拷掠，自誣言殺。

translations.literal: Di, fearing torture, falsely confessed that he had killed.
translations.idiomatic: Di, fearing torture, falsely confessed to the murder.

sentences.zh: 獄既至州，悅觀色察言，疑其不實。

translations.literal: When the case reached the province, Yue observed his expression and scrutinized his words and suspected it was not true.
translations.idiomatic: When the case reached the provincial court, Yue studied the man's manner and testimony and suspected the confession was false.

sentences.zh: 引見毛奴兄靈之，謂曰：「殺人取錢，當時狼狽，應有所遺，此賊竟遺何物？

translations.literal: He summoned and saw Maonu's elder brother Lingzhi and said to him: "In killing a man and taking money, one would have been flustered at the time and ought to have left something behind—what did this thief actually leave?"
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Maonu's elder brother Lingzhi and asked: "A killer seizing money would have been flustered at the scene and must have left something behind. What did this thief leave?"

sentences.zh: 」靈之云：「唯得一刀鞘而已。

translations.literal: " Lingzhi said: "Only a scabbard was obtained."
translations.idiomatic: " Lingzhi replied: "Only a sword scabbard."

sentences.zh: 」悅取鞘視之，曰：「此非里巷所為也。

translations.literal: " Yue took the scabbard and examined it, saying: "This is not the work of alley folk."
translations.idiomatic: Yue examined the scabbard and said: "This is not the sort of thing made in an ordinary neighborhood."

sentences.zh: 」乃召州城刀匠示之，有郭門者前曰：「此刀鞘門手所作，去歲賣與郭民董及祖。

translations.literal: " He then summoned the swordsmiths of the provincial city and showed it to them; one Guo Men stepped forward and said: "This scabbard was made by the craftsman Men; last year it was sold to the Guo commoner Dong Jizu."
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the city's swordsmiths. A man named Guo Men stepped forward and said: "This scabbard was made by the craftsman Men and was sold last year to a townsman named Dong Jizu."

sentences.zh: 」悅收及祖，詰之曰：「汝何故殺人取錢而遺刀鞘？

translations.literal: " Yue seized Jizu and interrogated him: "Why did you kill a man and take money yet leave the scabbard?"
translations.idiomatic: Yue arrested Jizu and demanded: "Why did you kill a man for his money and leave the scabbard behind?"

sentences.zh: 」及祖款引，靈之又於及祖身上得毛奴所著皂襦，及祖伏法。

translations.literal: " Jizu confessed in full; Lingzhi again obtained on Jizu's person the black jacket Maonu had worn, and Jizu was executed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Jizu confessed fully. Lingzhi then found on Jizu's person the black jacket Maonu had been wearing, and Jizu was executed.

sentences.zh: 悅之察獄，多此類也。

translations.literal: Yue's examination of prison cases was largely of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's handling of criminal cases was often of this sort.

sentences.zh: 豫州于今稱之。

translations.literal: Yu province still praises him for it today.
translations.idiomatic: Yu province still speaks of him with praise.

sentences.zh: 悅與鎮南將軍元英攻義陽，克之。

translations.literal: Yue together with General Who Guards the South Yuan Ying attacked Yiyang and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Yue joined General Who Guards the South Yuan Ying in attacking Yiyang and captured the city.

sentences.zh: 詔改蕭衍司州為郢州，以悅為征虜將軍、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict changed Xiao Yan's Si province to Ying province and made Yue General Who Captures Barbarians and Inspector of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: An edict renamed Xiao Yan's Si province as Ying and appointed Yue General Who Captures Barbarians and Inspector of Ying.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍遣其豫州刺史馬仙琕，左軍將軍、永陽戍主陳可等率眾一萬，於三關南六十里因山起城，名為竹敦，遣其輔國將軍、濟陰太守薊沛精卒二千以戍之。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan sent his Inspector of Yu Ma Xianbi, General of the Left Army and garrison commander of Yongyang Chen Ke and others leading ten thousand men; sixty li south of the Three Passes they built a city against the mountain called Zhudun, and sent his Aid-the-State General and Administrator of Jiyin Ji Pei with two thousand picked troops to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan sent his Inspector of Yu Ma Xianbi, General of the Left Army and Yongyang garrison commander Chen Ke, and others with ten thousand men to build a fortified town called Zhudun on a mountain sixty li south of the Three Passes, and posted his Aid-the-State General and Administrator of Jiyin Ji Pei there with two thousand elite troops.

sentences.zh: 後於關南四十里麻陽舊柵起城，仙琕輕騎東西為之節度。

translations.literal: Later, forty li south of the pass at the old stockade of Mayang they built a city; Xianbi with light cavalry directed affairs east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Later they built another town forty li south of the pass at the old Mayang stockade, while Xianbi rode back and forth with light cavalry to direct operations.

sentences.zh: 關南之民，多懷兩望。

translations.literal: The people south of the pass mostly harbored divided loyalties.
translations.idiomatic: The people south of the pass were largely torn between the two sides.

sentences.zh: 悅令西關統軍諸靈鳳掩擊，敗之，盡燔其城樓儲積，擒薊沛及其輔國將軍、軍主劉靈秀。

translations.literal: Yue ordered the commander of the Western Pass Zhu Lingfeng to strike by surprise, defeated them, burned all their tower stores, and captured Ji Pei together with his Aid-the-State General and army commander Liu Lingxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Yue ordered Zhu Lingfeng, commander of the Western Pass, to attack by surprise. The enemy was defeated, their stockpiled supplies in the towers were burned, and Ji Pei was captured along with his Aid-the-State General and army commander Liu Lingxiu.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「司馬悅首謀義陽，征略有捷。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Sima Yue first planned the Yiyang campaign, and the expedition had success."
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "Sima Yue first devised the plan for Yiyang, and the campaign met with success."

sentences.zh: 且違京既久，屢請入朝。

translations.literal: "Moreover, away from the capital long, he has repeatedly asked to enter court."
translations.idiomatic: "He has long been away from the capital and has repeatedly asked to attend court."

sentences.zh: 可遂此志，聽其赴闕。

translations.literal: "His wish may be fulfilled—let him come to the palace."
translations.idiomatic: "Let this wish be granted and allow him to come to court."

sentences.zh: 」尋詔以本將軍為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: " Soon an edict made him with his present rank Inspector of Yu province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward an edict appointed him Inspector of Yu while retaining his present rank.

sentences.zh: 論義陽之勳，封漁陽縣開國子，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Considering his merit at Yiyang, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Yuyang with a state fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit at Yiyang he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Yuyang with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 朏，尚世宗妹華陽公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Fei married Shizong's younger sister the Princess of Huayang and was appointed Commandant of the Feathered Forest for the Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: Fei married Emperor Xiaowen's younger sister, the Princess of Huayang, and was appointed Commandant of the Feathered Forest for the Imperial Son-in-Law.

sentences.zh: 特除員外散騎常侍，加鎮遠將軍。

translations.literal: He was specially appointed Extra Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and given the additional title General Who Pacifies the Distant.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially appointed Extra Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary with the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the Distant.

sentences.zh: 正光五年，公主薨。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengguang the princess died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhengguang the princess died.

sentences.zh: 月餘，朏卒。

translations.literal: After more than a month, Fei died.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a month later Fei died.

sentences.zh: 贈左將軍、滄州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded General of the Left and Inspector of Cang province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General of the Left and Inspector of Cang.

sentences.zh: 子鴻，字慶雲。

translations.literal: His son Hong, styled Qingyun.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hong, whose courtesy name was Qingyun.

sentences.zh: 性粗武。

translations.literal: His nature was rough and martial.
translations.idiomatic: He was rough and martial by nature.

sentences.zh: 襲爵，位至都水使者。

translations.literal: He inherited the title and reached the post of Commissioner of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title and rose to Commissioner of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 坐與西賊交通賜死。

translations.literal: For associating with western rebels he was sentenced to death by imperial gift.
translations.idiomatic: He was sentenced to death for communicating with western rebels.

sentences.zh: 子孝政，襲。

translations.literal: His son Xiaozheng inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaozheng inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the mandate, his title was reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne, his title was reduced in the usual way.

sentences.zh: 金龍弟躍，字寶龍。

translations.literal: Jinlong's younger brother Yue, styled Baolong.
translations.idiomatic: Jinlong's younger brother Yue, whose courtesy name was Baolong.

sentences.zh: 尚趙郡公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: He married the Princess of Zhao commandery and was appointed Commandant of the Feathered Forest for the Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: He married the Princess of Zhao commandery and was appointed Commandant of the Feathered Forest for the Imperial Son-in-Law.

sentences.zh: 代兄為雲中鎮將、朔州刺史，假安北將軍、河內公。

translations.literal: He replaced his elder brother as Garrison Commander of Yunzhong and Inspector of Shuo province, provisionally General Who Pacifies the North and Duke of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded his elder brother as Garrison Commander of Yunzhong and Inspector of Shuo, with provisional rank as General Who Pacifies the North and Duke of Henan.

sentences.zh: 躍表罷河西苑封，與民墾殖。

translations.literal: Yue memorialized to abolish the sealed park west of the river in Hexi and let the people open land for cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Yue memorialized to abolish the imperial park west of the Yellow River in Hexi and open the land to cultivation by the people.

sentences.zh: 有司執奏：「此麋鹿所聚，太官取給，今若與民，至於奉獻時禽，懼有所闕。

translations.literal: The responsible offices submitted firmly: "This is where deer gather; the Grand Provisioner draws supplies here—if it is now given to the people, when the time comes to present tribute birds and beasts, we fear there will be shortages."
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices objected: "This is where deer gather and the imperial kitchen draws its supply. If the land is given to the people, we fear there will be shortages when tribute animals are required for state sacrifices."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「此地若任稼穡，雖有獸利，事須廢封。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "If this place can bear grain crops, though there is benefit from beasts, the park must be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "If this land can bear crops, the park must be abolished even if it yields game."

sentences.zh: 若是山澗，虞禁何損？

translations.literal: "If it is mountain ravines, what harm is there in preserving the prohibition?"
translations.idiomatic: "If it is only mountain ravines, what harm is there in keeping the hunting preserve?"

sentences.zh: 尋先朝置此，豈苟藉斯禽，亮亦以俟軍行薪蒸之用。

translations.literal: "Investigating why the former court established this—not merely to rely on these beasts; clearly it was also to await fuel for army marches."
translations.idiomatic: "Consider why the former court established this preserve—it was not merely for the game, but also to supply firewood for military campaigns."

sentences.zh: 其更論之。

translations.literal: "Let the matter be discussed again."
translations.idiomatic: "Reconsider the matter."

sentences.zh: 」躍固請宜以與民，高祖從之。

translations.literal: " Yue firmly requested that it ought to be given to the people; Gaozu agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Yue insisted that the land should go to the people, and Emperor Xiaowen agreed.

sentences.zh: 還為祠部尚書、大鴻臚卿、潁川王師。

translations.literal: He returned to serve as Minister of the Imperial Clan, Grand Minister of Splendid Happiness, and Preceptor to the Prince of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as Minister of the Imperial Clan, Grand Minister of Splendid Happiness, and Preceptor to the Prince of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 以疾表求解任。

translations.literal: On grounds of illness he memorialized requesting release from office.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on grounds of illness to resign his posts.

sentences.zh: 太和十九年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the nineteenth year of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the nineteenth year of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 贈金紫光祿大夫，賜朝服一具、衣一襲、絹一千匹。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Gold Seal and given one set of court robes, one suit of clothes, and one thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Gold Seal and granted one set of court robes, one suit of clothes, and one thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 楚之父子相繼鎮雲中，朔土服其威德。

translations.literal: Chuzhi father and son in succession garrisoned Yunzhong; the Shuo region submitted to their authority and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhi and his son in succession held Yunzhong, and the Shuo region submitted to their authority and virtue.

sentences.zh: 司馬景之，字洪略，晉汝南王亮之後。

translations.literal: Sima Jingzhi, styled Honglue, was a descendant of Jin's Prince of Runan Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jingzhi, whose courtesy name was Honglue, was a descendant of Prince Liang of Runan of Jin.

sentences.zh: 太宗時歸闕，爵蒼梧公，加征南大將軍。

translations.literal: During Taizong's time he returned to court, was enfeoffed as Duke of Cangwu, and given the additional title Great General Who Conquers the South.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Mingyuan's reign he came to court, was enfeoffed as Duke of Cangwu, and made Great General Who Conquers the South.

sentences.zh: 清直有節操，太宗甚重之。

translations.literal: Pure, upright, and with integrity, Taizong greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and principled, he was highly esteemed by Emperor Mingyuan.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈汝南王。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously awarded Prince of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Runan.

sentences.zh: 子師子襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Shizi inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shizi inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 景之兄準，字巨之。

translations.literal: Jingzhi's elder brother Zhun, styled Juzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhi's elder brother Zhun, whose courtesy name was Juzhi.

sentences.zh: 以泰常末，率三千餘家歸國。

translations.literal: At the end of Taichang he led more than three thousand households to submit to the state.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Taichang era he led more than three thousand households to submit to Wei.

sentences.zh: 時太宗在虎牢，授寧遠將軍、新蔡公、假相州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time Taizong was at Hulao; he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distant, Duke of Xincai, and provisionally Inspector of Xiang province.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then at Hulao and appointed him General Who Pacifies the Distant, Duke of Xincai, and provisional Inspector of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 隨駕至京。

translations.literal: He followed the imperial carriage to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor to the capital.

sentences.zh: 出除廣寧太守。

translations.literal: He went out and was appointed Administrator of Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Administrator of Guangning.

sentences.zh: 悅近來遠，清儉有稱。

translations.literal: He delighted those near and drew those from afar; purity and frugality won him renown.
translations.idiomatic: He won the near and drew the distant through kindness, and was known for purity and frugality.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘉之，賜布六百匹。

translations.literal: Shizu commended him and bestowed six hundred bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him and granted six hundred bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 後降號為平遠將軍，改為密陵侯。

translations.literal: Later his rank was reduced to General Who Pacifies the Distant and changed to Marquis of Miling.
translations.idiomatic: Later his rank was reduced to General Who Pacifies the Distant and his title changed to Marquis of Miling.

sentences.zh: 興光初卒。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of Xingguang.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Xingguang era.

sentences.zh: 子安國襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Anguo inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Anguo inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 司馬叔璠，晉安平獻王孚之後也。

translations.literal: Sima Shufan was a descendant of Jin's Prince Xian of Anping Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shufan was a descendant of Prince Xian of Anping Fu of Jin.

sentences.zh: 父曇之，司馬德宗河間王。

translations.literal: His father Tanzhi was Sima Dezong's Prince of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tanzhi was Prince of Hejian under Emperor An of Jin.

sentences.zh: 桓玄、劉裕之際，叔璠與兄國璠北奔慕容超。

translations.literal: In the time of Huan Xuan and Liu Yu, Shufan and his elder brother Guofan fled north to Murong Chao.
translations.idiomatic: During the struggles of Huan Xuan and Liu Yu, Shufan and his elder brother Guofan fled north to Murong Chao.

sentences.zh: 後西投姚興。

translations.literal: Later they went west to submit to Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Later they went west and submitted to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 劉裕滅姚泓，北奔屈丐。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu destroyed Yao Hong, they fled north to Juqu Mugou.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu destroyed Yao Hong, they fled north to Juqu Mugou.

sentences.zh: 世祖平統萬，兄弟俱入國。

translations.literal: When Shizu pacified Tongwan, the brothers both entered the state.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor pacified Tongwan, both brothers entered Wei.

sentences.zh: [6]國璠賜爵淮南公。

translations.literal: [6] Guofan was granted the title Duke of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: [6] Guofan was enfeoffed as Duke of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 卒，無子，爵除。

translations.literal: He died without sons and the title was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He died without heirs and the title lapsed.

sentences.zh: 叔璠，安遠將軍、丹楊侯。

translations.literal: Shufan was General Who Pacifies the Distant and Marquis of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shufan was General Who Pacifies the Distant and Marquis of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 長子靈壽，神䴥中，與弟道壽俱來歸國。

translations.literal: His eldest son Lingshou, during Shenrui, came with his younger brother Daoshou together to submit to the state.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Lingshou, during the Shenrui era, came to Wei together with his younger brother Daoshou.

sentences.zh: 靈壽，冠軍將軍、溫縣侯；

translations.literal: Lingshou was Champion General and Marquis of Wen county;
translations.idiomatic: Lingshou was Champion General and Marquis of Wen county;

sentences.zh: 道壽，寧朔將軍、宜陽子。

translations.literal: Daoshou was General Who Pacifies the North and Viscount of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Daoshou was General Who Pacifies the North and Viscount of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 靈壽出除陳郡太守。

translations.literal: Lingshou went out and was removed as Administrator of Chen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lingshou was appointed Administrator of Chen commandery.

sentences.zh: 劉義隆侵境，詔靈壽招引義士，得二千餘人，從西平公安頡破虎牢、滑臺、洛陽三城，徙五百餘家入河內。

translations.literal: When Liu Yilong invaded the borders, an edict ordered Lingshou to recruit righteous men; he obtained more than two thousand and followed the Prince of Xiping An Bi in taking the three cities Hulao, Huatai, and Luoyang, relocating more than five hundred households into Henan.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yilong invaded the frontier, Lingshou was ordered to rally loyalists and gathered more than two thousand men. He followed Prince of Xiping An Bi in capturing Hulao, Huatai, and Luoyang and resettled more than five hundred households in Henan.

sentences.zh: 又從討蠕蠕，西征涼州，所在著功。

translations.literal: He also followed campaigns against the Rouran and the western expedition to Liang province, achieving merit wherever he went.
translations.idiomatic: He also joined campaigns against the Rouran and the western expedition to Liangzhou, distinguishing himself in each.

sentences.zh: 出為遼西太守，治有清儉之稱。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Liaoxi; in governance he had a reputation for purity and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Administrator of Liaoxi, where his rule won renown for purity and frugality.

sentences.zh: 太和九年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the ninth year of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 贈懷州刺史，諡曰靖。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Inspector of Huai province with posthumous name Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Inspector of Huai with the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 靈壽娶太宰、頓丘王李峻女，與婦父雅不相善，每見抑退，故位不大至。

translations.literal: Lingshou married the daughter of the Grand Mentor and Prince of Dunqiu Li Jun; with his wife's father he was on poor terms by nature and was repeatedly held back and demoted, and therefore his rank did not rise high.
translations.idiomatic: Lingshou married the daughter of Grand Mentor and Prince of Dunqiu Li Jun. He was on poor terms with his father-in-law, who repeatedly held him back, and so he never rose to high office.

sentences.zh: 子惠安，高祖時襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Huian, during Gaozu's time, inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huian inherited the title under Emperor Xiaowen.

sentences.zh: 歷恒州別駕、桑乾太守、太尉諮議參軍事。

translations.literal: He successively served as Administrator's Assistant of Heng province, Administrator of Sanggan, and Consulting Army Officer of the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Administrator's Assistant of Heng, Administrator of Sanggan, and Consulting Army Officer under the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子祖珍，年十五，舉司州秀才。

translations.literal: His son Zuzhen, at age fifteen, was nominated as a provincial graduate of Si.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zuzhen, at fifteen, was nominated as a Si province graduate.

sentences.zh: 解褐員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: On leaving the sackcloth he was appointed Extra Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: On entering office he was appointed Extra Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 年十八，先父卒。

translations.literal: At age eighteen he died before his father.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighteen, predeceasing his father.

sentences.zh: 祖珍弟宗龐，世宗時，父惠安以久病啟以爵轉授。

translations.literal: Zuzhen's younger brother Zongpang, during Shizong's time, because father Huian's long illness memorialized to transfer the title to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zuzhen's younger brother Zongpang, under Emperor Xiaowen, received the title when his father Huian, long ill, memorialized to transfer it to him.

sentences.zh: 解褐安定王府騎兵參軍，洛州龍驤府司馬。

translations.literal: On leaving the sackcloth he was Cavalry Army Officer of the Prince of Anding's establishment and Staff Officer of the Dragon Cavalry Command of Luo province.
translations.idiomatic: On entering office he was Cavalry Army Officer in the establishment of the Prince of Anding and Staff Officer of the Dragon Cavalry Command of Luo.

sentences.zh: 善射，未曾自伐。

translations.literal: Skilled in archery, he never boasted of himself.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in archery but never boasted of it.

sentences.zh: 性閑淡，少所交遊。

translations.literal: His nature was leisurely and detached; he had few social connections.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was quiet and detached, with few companions.

sentences.zh: 識者云其淳至。

translations.literal: Observers said his nature was pure and sincere.
translations.idiomatic: Those who knew him said he was utterly sincere.

sentences.zh: 永安中卒。

translations.literal: He died during Yongan.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Yongan era.

sentences.zh: 子嵩亮襲。

translations.literal: His son Songliang inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Songliang inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 惠安弟直安，歷位尚書郎，濟北、濟南二郡太守，員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Huian's younger brother Zhian successively held the posts of Secretariat Gentleman, Administrator of the two commanderies Jibei and Jinan, and Extra Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Huian's younger brother Zhian served in turn as Secretariat Gentleman, Administrator of Jibei and Jinan, and Extra Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶夤征鍾離，引為長史。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin campaigned against Zhongli, he was brought in as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Baoyin campaigned against Zhongli, Zhian was appointed his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 坐軍退，免官加刑。

translations.literal: For the army's retreat he was dismissed from office and punished.
translations.idiomatic: Because the army retreated he was stripped of office and punished.

sentences.zh: 以疾得免。

translations.literal: On grounds of illness he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: He was spared punishment on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 尋除東平原太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Administrator of Dongpingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Administrator of Dongpingyuan.

sentences.zh: 還京，為中散大夫，加征虜將軍、太中大夫，遷左將軍。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, he was made Palace Attendant, given the additional titles General Who Captures Barbarians and Grand Master of the Palace, and transferred to General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to the capital he became Palace Attendant, was given the additional ranks of General Who Captures Barbarians and Grand Master of the Palace, and was promoted to General of the Left.

sentences.zh: 正光四年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Zhengguang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Zhengguang.

sentences.zh: 贈大將軍、濟州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Great General and Inspector of Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Great General and Inspector of Ji.

sentences.zh: 子龍泉，滄州開府長史。

translations.literal: His son Longquan was Chief Clerk of the Cangzhou headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: His son Longquan was chief clerk of the Cangzhou headquarters.

sentences.zh: 道壽長子元興，襲父爵。

translations.literal: Daoshou's eldest son Yuanxing inherited his father's title.
translations.idiomatic: Daoshou's eldest son Yuanxing inherited his father's title.

sentences.zh: 子景和，給事中，稍遷揚州驃騎府長史、清河內史。

translations.literal: His son Jinghe was Attendant Within the Yellow Gates, then gradually transferred to Chief Clerk of Yangzhou's Rapid-as-Steed Headquarters and Interior Secretary of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jinghe was Attendant Within the Yellow Gates and later rose to chief clerk of Yangzhou's Rapid-as-Steed Headquarters and Interior Secretary of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 正光元年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Zhengguang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Zhengguang.

sentences.zh: 贈左將軍、平州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded General of the Left and Inspector of Ping province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General of the Left and Inspector of Ping.

sentences.zh: 元興弟仲明，侍御史、中書舍人。

translations.literal: Yuanxing's younger brother Zhongming was Attending Censor and Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxing's younger brother Zhongming served as Attending Censor and Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 以謹敏著稱。

translations.literal: He was known for prudence and alertness.
translations.idiomatic: He was known for prudence and tact.

sentences.zh: 稍遷衞尉少卿，仍領舍人。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to Vice Minister of the Guard and still headed the drafters.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Minister of the Guard while continuing to head the secretariat drafters.

sentences.zh: 出為征虜將軍、涼州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Captures Barbarians and Inspector of Liang province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Captures Barbarians and Inspector of Liang.

sentences.zh: 坐貪殘，為御史所彈，遇赦免，積年不敍。

translations.literal: For greed and cruelty he was impeached by the censorate, met an amnesty and was spared, and for many years received no reinstatement.
translations.idiomatic: For greed and cruelty he was impeached by the censorate, was spared by an amnesty, and went unreinstated for many years.

sentences.zh: 後娶靈太后從姊為繼室，除武衞將軍、征虜將軍。

translations.literal: Later he married Empress Dowager Ling's cousin as his second wife and was appointed General of Martial Guards and General Who Captures Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Later he married a cousin of Empress Dowager Ling as his second wife and was made General of Martial Guards and General Who Captures Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 轉光祿大夫，武衞如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness while keeping Martial Guards as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness while retaining his post as General of Martial Guards.

sentences.zh: 遷大司農卿，加安東將軍、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Grand Granaries and given the additional titles General Who Pacifies the East and Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Grand Granaries with the additional ranks of General Who Pacifies the East and Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 出為安北將軍、恒州刺史，常侍如故。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Heng province, with Cavalier Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Heng while retaining his rank as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 正光五年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the fifth year of Zhengguang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Zhengguang.

sentences.zh: 子彥邕，有風望。

translations.literal: His son Yanyong had reputation and bearing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanyong enjoyed reputation and prestige.

sentences.zh: 正員郎。

translations.literal: Regular Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was a regular secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 稍遷相州刺史、驃騎大將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to Inspector of Xiang province, Great General of Rapid-as-Steed Cavalry, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness on the Left.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Inspector of Xiang, Great General of Rapid-as-Steed Cavalry, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness on the Left.

sentences.zh: 天平四年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Tianping.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Tianping.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍、都督懷洛二州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、懷州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Huai and Luo provinces, Great General of Rapid-as-Steed Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Huai province.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, commander of military affairs in Huai and Luo, Great General of Rapid-as-Steed Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Huai.

sentences.zh: 司馬天助，自云司馬德宗驃騎將軍元顯之子。

translations.literal: Sima Tianzhu claimed himself to be the son of Sima Dezong's Rapid-as-Steed General Yuan Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Tianzhu claimed to be the son of Rapid-as-Steed General Yuan Xian, who served under Emperor An of Jin.

sentences.zh: 劉裕自立，乃來歸闕。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu declared himself emperor, he then came to submit at court.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Yu seized the throne he came to court and submitted.

sentences.zh: [7]除平東將軍、青徐二州刺史、東海公。

translations.literal: [7] He was appointed General Who Pacifies the East, Inspector of Qing and Xu provinces, and Duke of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: [7] He was made General Who Pacifies the East, Inspector of Qing and Xu, and Duke of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 天助招率義士，欲襲裕東平、濟北二郡及城戍，又破裕將閭萬齡軍，前後多所虜獲。

translations.literal: Tianzhu recruited righteous men, intended to strike Yu's two commanderies Dongping and Jibei and their garrison towns, and again defeated Yu's general Yan Wanling's army, capturing much in successive actions.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzhu rallied loyalists and planned to strike Liu Yu's commanderies of Dongping and Jibei and their garrisons. He also defeated the army of Liu Yu's general Yan Wanling and took many captives and spoils.

sentences.zh: 拜侍中、都督青徐兗三州諸軍事、征東將軍、青兗二州刺史，公如故。

translations.literal: He was appointed Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Qing, Xu, and Yan provinces, General Who Conquers the East, and Inspector of Qing and Yan provinces, with his ducal title unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Palace Attendant, commander of military affairs in Qing, Xu, and Yan, General Who Conquers the East, and Inspector of Qing and Yan, retaining his ducal title.

sentences.zh: 真君三年，與司馬文思等南討。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenjun he joined Sima Wensi and others in the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenjun he joined Sima Wensi and others on the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 還，又從駕北征。

translations.literal: On return he again followed the imperial carriage on the northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he again accompanied the emperor on the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 在陣歿。

translations.literal: He died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He died in battle.

sentences.zh: 子元伯，字歸都。

translations.literal: His son Yuanbo, styled Guidu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanbo, whose courtesy name was Guidu.

sentences.zh: 襲爵，後降溫縣子。

translations.literal: He inherited the title and later was reduced to Viscount of Wen county.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title and was later reduced to Viscount of Wen county.

sentences.zh: 太和中，為建威將軍、泰山太守。

translations.literal: During Taihe he was General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era he was General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Taishan.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：諸司馬以亂亡歸命。

translations.literal: The historian writes: The various Sima clansmen submitted in the disorder of ruin.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: The various Sima clansmen came to submit amid the chaos of dynastic collapse.

sentences.zh: 楚之風概器略，最可稱乎？

translations.literal: Of Chuzhi's bearing and strategic capacity—is he not the most praiseworthy?
translations.idiomatic: Of them all, is not Chuzhi's spirit and strategic talent the most worthy of praise?

sentences.zh: 其餘未足論也。

translations.literal: The rest are not worth discussing.
translations.idiomatic: The rest scarcely merit discussion.

sentences.zh: 而以往代遺緒，並當位遇。

translations.literal: Yet as surviving threads of former dynasties, all received rank and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as remnants of a former dynasty, they all received rank and favor.

sentences.zh: 可謂幸矣。

translations.literal: This may be called fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: They were fortunate indeed.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 晉宣帝季弟譙王遜之後也 南本以下諸本及北史卷二九司馬休之傳「遜」作「進」。

translations.literal: "Descendant of Prince of Qiao Sima Yi, the younger brother of the fourth rank of Jin's Emperor Xuan": in the Southern edition and all editions below, and in Beishi juan 29 biography of Sima Xiuzhi, "Yi" (遜) is written "Jin" (進).
translations.idiomatic: "A descendant of Prince of Qiao Sima Yi": in the Southern edition and later editions, and in the Beishi biography of Sima Xiuzhi (juan 29), "Yi" is written as "Jin."

sentences.zh: 百衲本作「遜」，汲、局二本注宋本作「遜」。

translations.literal: The Patchwork edition has "Yi"; the Ji and Bureau editions' notes on the Song edition also have "Yi."
translations.idiomatic: The Patchwork edition reads "Yi"; the Ji and Bureau editions' notes on the Song edition also read "Yi."

sentences.zh: 錢氏考異卷二八、李慈銘魏書札記、張森楷魏書校勘記各有說。

translations.literal: Qian's Textual Variants juan 28, Li Ciming's Notes on the Book of Wei, and Zhang Senkai's Collation of the Book of Wei each have explanations.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's Textual Variants (juan 28), Li Ciming's Notes on the Book of Wei, and Zhang Senkai's Collation of the Book of Wei each discuss the point.

sentences.zh: 按晉書卷三七譙王遜傳，遜是進子，進死於曹魏時，封譙王的是遜，不是進。

translations.literal: According to Jinshu juan 37 biography of Prince of Qiao Sima Yi, Yi was Jin's son; Jin died in Cao-Wei times, and the one enfeoffed as Prince of Qiao was Yi, not Jin.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Jinshu biography of Prince of Qiao Sima Yi (juan 37), Yi was Jin's son. Jin died in the Cao-Wei period, and it was Yi who was enfeoffed as Prince of Qiao, not Jin.

sentences.zh: 但進才是晉宣帝司馬懿季弟，遜是從子，作「遜」也有問題。

translations.literal: But only Jin was the younger brother of the fourth rank of Jin's Emperor Xuan Sima Yi; Yi was a nephew—writing "Yi" also has problems.
translations.idiomatic: Yet only Jin was the younger brother of Jin's Emperor Xuan, Sima Yi; Yi was a nephew. Writing "Yi" is also problematic.

sentences.zh: 作「進」作「遜」既都有問題，而宋本作「遜」，恐原來就錯。

translations.literal: Whether written "Jin" or "Yi" both have problems, yet the Song edition has "Yi"—probably the original was already wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Whether one writes "Jin" or "Yi" both are problematic, yet the Song edition reads "Yi"—the original text was probably already in error.

sentences.zh: 此卷史實上的謬誤較多，疑有訛脫竄亂，非魏收原文。

translations.literal: This juan has rather many factual errors; it is suspected there are corruptions, omissions, and interpolations—not Wei Shou's original text.
translations.idiomatic: This chapter contains many factual errors and is suspected of corruption, omission, and interpolation—not Wei Shou's original text.

sentences.zh: 為懷朔鎮將 北史卷二九「懷朔」作「懷荒」。

translations.literal: "Made Garrison Commander of Huaishuo": in Beishi juan 29 "Huaishuo" is written "Huaihuang."
translations.idiomatic: "Made garrison commander of Huaishuo": in the Beishi (juan 29) "Huaishuo" is written as "Huaihuang."

sentences.zh: 按卷三九李寶傳云：「高宗初，代司馬文思鎮懷荒。

translations.literal: According to juan 39 biography of Li Bao: "At the beginning of Gaozong's reign, he replaced Sima Wensi in garrisoning Huaihuang."
translations.idiomatic: According to the biography of Li Bao (juan 39): "Early in Emperor Gaozong's reign he replaced Sima Wensi as garrison commander of Huaihuang."

sentences.zh: 」北史是，這裏作「懷朔」誤。

translations.literal: " The Beishi is correct; writing "Huaishuo" here is an error.
translations.idiomatic: The Beishi is correct; "Huaishuo" here is an error.

sentences.zh: 以楚之所率戶民分置汝南南陽南頓新蔡四郡 北史卷二九「南陽」作「汝陽」。

translations.literal: "The household population Chuzhi led was distributed into the four commanderies Runan, Nanyang, Nandun, and Xincai": in Beishi juan 29 "Nanyang" is written "Ruyang."
translations.idiomatic: "The households Chuzhi led were settled in Runan, Nanyang, Nandun, and Xincai": in the Beishi (juan 29) "Nanyang" is written as "Ruyang."

sentences.zh: 按宋書卷三六州郡志豫州有「汝陽」，無「南陽」。

translations.literal: According to Songshu juan 36 Treatise on Provinces and Commanderies, Yu province has "Ruyang" and not "Nanyang."
translations.idiomatic: According to the Songshu Treatise on Provinces and Commanderies (juan 36), Yu province had "Ruyang" and not "Nanyang."

sentences.zh: 當時僑置亦必因豫州原有此郡，疑作「汝陽」是。

translations.literal: The refugee establishment at that time must also have followed Yu province's having this commandery originally—"Ruyang" is probably correct.
translations.idiomatic: The refugee commandery was probably named for an existing Yu province district; "Ruyang" is likely correct.

sentences.zh: 永平元年 諸本「平」作「元」。

translations.literal: "First year of Yongping": in all editions "ping" is written "yuan."
translations.idiomatic: "First year of Yongping": in all editions "ping" is written as "yuan."

sentences.zh: 按事見卷八世宗紀永平元年十月，今據北史卷二九司馬悅傳改。

translations.literal: The event is seen in juan 8 Annals of Shizong, tenth month of the first year of Yongping; the text now follows Beishi juan 29 biography of Sima Yue in correction.
translations.idiomatic: The event appears in the Annals of Emperor Xiaowen (juan 8), tenth month of the first year of Yongping. The text is now corrected following the Beishi biography of Sima Yue (juan 29).

sentences.zh: 劉裕滅姚泓北奔屈丐世祖平統萬兄弟俱入國 按卷三太宗紀泰常三年

translations.literal: "When Liu Yu destroyed Yao Hong they fled north to Juqu Mugou; when Shizu pacified Tongwan the brothers both entered the state": according to juan 3 Annals of Taizong, third year of Taichang
translations.idiomatic: "When Liu Yu destroyed Yao Hong they fled north to Juqu Mugou; when the emperor pacified Tongwan both brothers entered Wei": see the Annals of Emperor Mingyuan (juan 3), third year of Taichang

sentences.zh: 〈四一七〉
八月劉裕滅姚泓，九月癸酉記司馬休之父子及國璠等「來降」。

translations.literal: eighth month Liu Yu destroyed Yao Hong; ninth month guiyou day records Sima Xiuzhi father and sons and Guofan and others "came to surrender."
translations.idiomatic: in the eighth month Liu Yu destroyed Yao Hong; on the guiyou day of the ninth month it records that Sima Xiuzhi, his sons, Guofan, and others "came to surrender."

sentences.zh: 泰常五年五月即記國璠被殺。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taichang, fifth month, it immediately records Guofan was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth year of Taichang it records that Guofan was killed.

sentences.zh: 拓跋燾平統萬，事在始光四年

translations.literal: Tuoba Tao pacified Tongwan, the event being in the fourth year of Shiguang
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Tao pacified Tongwan, an event of the fourth year of Shiguang

sentences.zh: 〈四二七〉
，國璠已先死八年。

translations.literal: , and Guofan had already died eight years earlier.
translations.idiomatic: , by which time Guofan had been dead for eight years.

sentences.zh: 下文又稱國璠卒，一字不及被殺，却見於此卷司馬文思傳。

translations.literal: Below it again says Guofan died—not one word about being killed—yet it appears in this juan's biography of Sima Wensi.
translations.idiomatic: Below, Guofan's death is mentioned without a word about his execution, yet his killing appears in this chapter's biography of Sima Wensi.

sentences.zh: 也可怪。

translations.literal: This too is strange.
translations.idiomatic: This too is strange.

sentences.zh: 劉裕自立乃來歸闕 張森楷云：「帝紀

translations.literal: "When Liu Yu declared himself [emperor] he then came to submit at court": Zhang Senkai says: "Imperial annals
translations.idiomatic: "After Liu Yu seized the throne he came to submit": Zhang Senkai notes: "In the imperial annals

sentences.zh: 〈卷四上世祖紀上〉

translations.literal: (juan 4, upper, Annals of Shizu, part 1)"
translations.idiomatic: (Annals of Emperor Taiwu, part 1, juan 4)"

sentences.zh: 延和二年司馬天助來降，於宋為元嘉十年

translations.literal: second year of Yanhe Sima Tianzhu came to surrender; in Song this was the tenth year of Yuanjia
translations.idiomatic: in the second year of Yanhe Sima Tianzhu came to surrender—in the Liu Song calendar this was the tenth year of Yuanjia

sentences.zh: 〈四三三〉
，代晉久矣。

translations.literal: , and Jin had long been replaced.
translations.idiomatic: , by which time the Jin dynasty had long since fallen.

sentences.zh: 此文殊疏略。

translations.literal: This text is extremely loose and brief.
translations.idiomatic: This passage is remarkably careless.

sentences.zh: 」按下文稱天助「招率義士，欲襲裕東平、濟北郡及城戍，又破裕將閭萬齡軍」，「裕」字皆誤。

translations.literal: " Investigating below, which says Tianzhu "recruited righteous men, intended to strike Yu's commanderies Dongping and Jibei and garrison towns, and again defeated Yu's general Yan Wanling's army"—every character "Yu" is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: " He adds that below, where Tianzhu "rallied loyalists, planned to strike Dongping and Jibei and their garrisons, and defeated the army of Liu Yu's general Yan Wanling," every instance of "Yu" is an error.
